Does the new dishwasher work? Yep! There will still be some water on top of mugs, but all plates, bowls, and silverware have been clean and dry when they come out. You can pay hundreds of dollars more to get better finishes and a quieter dishwasher, but it wasn't worth it for us.How was installation? We bought through Costco because installation was included. Sentence (English): We are a long-time Bosch Dishwasher family, having the same brand serve our kitchens for the last 30+ years.
Comments (English): [ Great cleaning-Top controls are very limited ] || ---------------- || We are a long-time Bosch Dishwasher family, having the same brand serve our kitchens for the last 30+ years. We recently decided to upgrade our 14 year old 500 series dishwasher and reviewed the latest line up. We decided to go for the 800 series for its advanced cleaning capabilities such as selecting zones for heavy cleaning, the additional sound insulation and the more efficient racks.On the cleaning and sound font, Bosch did not dissapoint. The dishes come out sparkling clean, and even pots that used to come out with some residue are now cleaner than what I would do by hand! My gripes are with the controls. The top controls are fewer than the less expensive models, and some of the most useful features are now in the mobile app only. A basic function such as a delayed start, needs to be run from the mobile app. Selecting the delicate mode (for crystal glasses) requires again the mobile app. No one in the house wants to load a mobile app for the dishwasher! This is really silly and needs to be on the dishwasher control panel.Lastly, the simplicity of interrupting the wash is gone. Before, you could just open the washer, add another plate, close the door and go. Now, you need to basically press start again, and close within 4 seconds! Why complicate the matters? In hindsight, I would likely make the trade off for a slightly lower price and slightly louder (46 db vs 42) washer that had more control buttons, than this model.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is incredibly quiet such that even standing a few feet away it is difficult to hear whether it is still running.
Comments (English): [ Incredibly quiet and very attractive ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is incredibly quiet such that even standing a few feet away it is difficult to hear whether it is still running. Fortunately the machine has a front status light which indicates whether it is still running or has completed the cycle. The racks are well designed to hold common kitchen items securely. With a previous dishwasher I could not get a dinner plate to stand upright- they kept tipping over and leaning against the plate in the next slot.I probably should have selected a cheaper model as this model has features that I won't use. It has a 3rd rack which I don't use. This 3rd rack also has a removable silverware holder which I removed because it just holds a lot of water causing drying problems.The racks slide in and out easily, the interior is stainless, the top mounted controls are easy to see and use and there is a display in the controls that tells you how long the cycle will run (in minutes) depending on the options selected. The only issue I have with the unit is that I'm having trouble getting the dishes to dry completely. Most dishwashers have a vent through which the moist air from the inside is vented to the outside to facilitate drying but I can't find a vent on this model. I've tried several combinations of options and so far have only been able to get the dishes about 85% dry. I suspect that I need to use the Dry Boost = High option but selecting this results in a cycle time of almost 4 hours. A 1 hour wash cycle with a Dry Boost = Normal results in a cycle time of almost 3 hours. On my previous dishwasher a quick wash with heated dry took about 1 hour and these settings resulted in clean dishes that were bone dry at the end of cycle.The door is perfectly balanced so if I want to leave the door open say 1 inch to finish drying the dishes the door stays 1 inch open and doesn't fall open.The manual for this dishwasher is poor. Part of the problem is general to all manufacturers in that they try to provide 1 manual for several models in the same family with frequent footnotes such as "if so equipped" or "on some models". I installed this dishwasher myself having done several in the past. Going step by step when almost done I came to the instruction to install the trim pieces. I spent about 10 minutes unsuccessfully looking for the trim pieces. I then started from the beginning of the instructions and noticed that under the trim pieces was the notation "on some models". Apparently trim pieces are not provided for this model. Removing the foot pads from the shipping crate required an odd sized socket that neither of my socket sets had. The screws to affix the toe kick are not included and the screw size isn't specified in the instructions. The included drain hose extension is only 5ft rather than the standard 6 feet which might be too short if your sink is to the right of the dishwasher.This model (GDT670SYVFS) is the finger print resistant model. If I had it to do over I'd probably get the stainless rather than the fingerprint resistant stainless model. The finger print resistant model is considered by GE to be a painted finish which has some very restrictive cleaning restrictions and it isn't very clear what the restrictions are. Basically you can only use a damp cloth with a mild soap. Counter intuitively you can not use a stainless steel cleaner on this fingerprint resistant stainless steel.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is sooooo quiet, I'm happily surprised.
Comments (English): The dishwasher is sooooo quiet, I'm happily surprised. I like how I can see the remaining time of the cycle on the top of the door, even when it's closed. When I was shopping for a dishwasher, I thought I'd have to get one with the control panel in front, but I couldn't find anything I wanted. But this one has the control panel on top. I can see the time and most of the other options/lights when the door is closed and washing. I really like the extra top rack. I used to wash my knives by hand because I didn't want them hitting other silverware. But now I can put them all on the top rack. The smaller knives I can even place blade side down in the holder. If I use the normal wash and normal dry boost, it takes 2 hours and 5 minutes. When it's done, the motor doesn't continue to run. (My previous dishwasher would still run the motor after the cycle was over.)

In hindsight, I would likely make the trade off for a slightly lower price and slightly louder (46 db vs 42) washer that had more control buttons, than this model.

After removing one of the two baskets I was able to load the dishawasher more easily and was absolutely delighted with how quiet it was and how well it washed the dishes. Then, in January of 2024, hours before a party was about to begin, the buttons on the front panel stopped working. I could turn it on, but couldn't start it. The folks that man Bosch's customer service line are just great! Unfortunately, while the circuit board was covered, the labor was not, and the labor was almost as expensive as the dishwasher was. Thankfully, after hanging up with Bosh, I remembered I had purchased an extended warranty from the retailer, and was able to get parts and labor at no cost. The repair folks were as great as Bosch's customer service, but unfortunately after two trips and a complete replacement of the circuit board and panel, the dishwasher ultimately had to be replaced, a mere 2.5 years after purchasing it, which seems pretty disappointing for a Bosch dishwasher. That said, even though I didn't love the design of the racks in this machine or its longevity, I did ultimately decide to purchase another Bosch. However, this time I went for the 300 series and am already impressed with the third rack and even quieter design.

Comments (English): [ Obsessed ] || ---------------- || I am in love with this dishwasher! I maybe love it too much. LOL It is exciting to unload my dishes and wow at how clean they are. The cleaning arm that moves in multple directions3. The variety of settings4. How quiet it is! My family kept opening it to put dishes in when the dishwasher was running, because they couldn't hear/tell it was in a wash cycle. There is a red light that stays on and shines on the floor when it is running, so that helps. 5. The connectivity. The app alerts me to any problems that arise during a wash cycle (like a dish or utensil blocking a wash arm) and lets me know when the cycle is complete. The dishwasher can also be turned on remotely from the app.6. It's gorgeous inside and out7. The customization of the racks is awesome! The middle rack has two levels it can be at, and the top silverwear rack has drop down functions on each side to provide for more room as needed.8. It comes with a silverwear basket, but it really isn't needed with how useful the top rack is. I'm glad that I have a basket option if needed, however.9. The plate prongs on the bottom rack hold plates perfectly in place and perfectly apart so that they can get clean. 10. Prongs can be laid down of lifted up om bottom and middle racks to fit your needs.11. The prongs and racks are a strong METAL. My previous dishwasher had weak prongs that were prone to breakage.12. The door is heavy and shuts tight.13. Having the control panel on the top end of the door prevents me or my kids from accidently bumping into buttons and starting or ending a cycle inadvertantly.14. I'm happy that this model comes in white; I prefer white over the cold-look and fingerprint prone stainless steel.15. I was told by the installer that this model is one of the longest lasting dishwashers.16. I'd buy this again in a heartbeat. I've had it about 5-6 weeks now, and I still get giddy over this dishwasher. LOL

Overall, it's pretty disappointing as one would expect more from the GE dishwasher.

It keeps coming out from the rubber packing, and I wiped it before spinning it, but it can't come out every time unless it melts inside the product. How can black organic matter come out when I only spin the transparent bottle and nipple that have been washed once? You said you couldn't provide any evidence for the test, sent me a few lines of a document, and charged me 50,000 won for the inspection, but we plan to respond soon. I'm leaving it five stars because I think you should look into the black substance and defects in this product and the customer service center response on Chefbon. Also, this post has no other purpose than public interest. Looking at the reviews, it seems I'm not the only one with black powder coming out, and that the customer service center has their service blocked, and even when black substances come out, they're responding by saying it's because of the detergent and that no exchanges or refunds are possible. Black foreign substances keep coming out of the rubber packing inside the dishwasher, and no matter how much I wipe it, it keeps coming out, and it seems to mix with the water and gets on the bottom where the water collects. I was using it because it was marketed as a baby bottle, but I'm so resentful that I'm continuing to use this product and feed it to my baby. The customer service center blocks calls and customers can't call first (they say they're doing maintenance, but since the customer service center is making calls, it seems like they're just blocking calls so that customers can't call. It's a separate matter for the buyer, and I guess they're having a hard time dealing with the numerous after-sales service calls). They say that the black powder coming off is probably a detergent problem, but if it's not hydrochloric acid, but a type 1 dishwasher-specific detergent that's causing the parts to come off and make powder fly, then it's a product defect. (I've tried running it without detergent several times, but it's still the same. It's just corroded water.) I also use a dishwasher from another company, so I've been using the same detergent for Chefborn at the recommended dosage for several years, and I've never had a problem. The ingredients are not corrosive to plastic or rubber, even when combined with high temperatures. They told me to bring it in for an internal inspection, but since there was definitely black powder coming from the product and I have evidence, I told them to pay for the installation and removal costs or come pick it up myself. They said that since I installed it myself, they wouldn't accept that and that I wouldn't be compensated for any damage caused by the black powder I've been eating. Even after seeing the evidence of the black powder, they say it's a detergent problem. Do you think they'll accept the problem by recalling the product? I asked about the process, and they said the inspection process involves taking it in, adding the detergent we use, and inspecting it. Of course, they'd try running it with a detergent that doesn't produce powder. If a specific product doesn't produce black powder, but other dishwasher detergents do, is that a legitimate product? They're making the product like this, and they're blaming the buyer for the detergent they use, and the buyer has to pay for all the shipping and packaging costs for the defective product. Personally, I think I made the worst choice when I think about my health, time, and hygiene. If you have the unidentified black substance and evidence, I hope you will accept an exchange, refund, or inspection and take it to the customer center and respond properly. *******I tried running it without detergent as the customer center told me, but it's the same. It just dissolves in the water and comes out. I wiped the nipple of my baby's bottle and it came out. I'm going crazy. It comes out every time. (***In addition, I found out that other users had the black powder issue, so I'm attaching it.) The customer center doesn't answer the phone, and I called during their available times, and after seeing other people's reviews with the same problem, they said there was definitely no problem and I'm going to send it back, but I'm wondering what to do.

Sentence (English): My dishes get wonderfully clean and it is pretty quiet, can hear water filling/draining and sometimes dishes rattling, but is not at all disturbing.
Comments (English): [ Works fine, but liked my old one better ] || ---------------- || My dishes get wonderfully clean and it is pretty quiet, can hear water filling/draining and sometimes dishes rattling, but is not at all disturbing. Plastics do not always get dry even with the chrystal dry so I don't really know if that option is worth it. I had a 800 series from 2011 (SHE68E15US) and I much preferred the top drawer silverware rack and silverware basket on that one. There is a weird piece on the top drawer handle that contantly pops off and the silverware just doesn't sit as well in this one as the old one, not sure why. I also don't think it holds as much silverware as my old one did. The cutlery basket is significantly smaller on the new one, I wish I would have kept the old basket before they hauled it away. Our previous one also had a delay start in the door controls, this one does not, however you can do a delay start on the app but it is a bit of a pain. I wish the app had an option to "start now" as opposed to having to set a start time; you can slide the time bar all the way over to the current time and it will start but a "start now" option would be a lot easier. (for those time you go to bed an remember you forgot to start this dishwasher! ) Overall it's a fine dishwasher. I think the app need quite a bit of work to make it more efficient to use, nobody wants to spend an extra couple of minutes in an app just to delay start the dishwasher

Sentence (English): We've had the Benchmark series for about a month and so far I love it.
Comments (English): [ Wonderful so far ] || ---------------- || We've had the Benchmark series for about a month and so far I love it. It has so many features it's crazy. I'll admit, I'm not a huge fan of having to connect to wifi for some of the features, but I also appreciate how cumbersome that would be to try to have it all be accessible on the machine itself. It's also pretty funny to get a message that your dishes are done going down the freeway 20 miles from home. I actually love the light inside. I thought it would be one of those superfluous features that I could take or leave but wow, what a difference it actually makes. I had a 300 series for over 10 years that still worked but was starting to lose some of its cleaning power, probably due to the hard water in our area. This thing cleans like a beast! And the dishes, when using rinse aid and crystal dry are very dry. Such an upgrade in every way from the 300. One negative is for the first week or so it had a very strong hot tar smell when it heated up during the cycle. I learned this is likely from the bitumen they use to encapsulate the body for soundproofing. It has dissipated, though still faintly there. My husband can't smell it at all. Still, a little troubling at first because I thought something was melting or on fire! Other than that, I'm super pleased with my purchase. 9/10 would buy again (loses a bit for the smell but not enough to keep me from buying it again).

Sentence (English): This dishwasher replaces a Bosch that we installed in 2010—it still worked but was showing the wear and tear of doing over 5,000 washes!
Comments (English): [ Awesome machine with 2 trivial drawbacks ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher replaces a Bosch that we installed in 2010—it still worked but was showing the wear and tear of doing over 5,000 washes! If anything, this Bosch 800 model is even quieter than the old one. The red light on the floor is often the only way we know it is running. The three-rack loading system is superb and very flexible. We love being able to lay flatware and small items in the top rack knowing they will stay there and get clean. The rinse aid dispenser and detergent dispenser are much improved from the earlier model, as they both stay closed until they are supposed to open (the rinse aid door failed after a year on our old machine).A couple of minuses: let's call the installation "brutally efficient". The boys came in and shoehorned the machine into its new space (which was custom built) by tearing a metal side panel off. They clearly had done this before, and the dishwasher hopefully didn't need that panel. Costco contracts this work out, and still doesn't have a firm handle on who and how it is done, so I would advise that you be present, ask questions, and stop them if they look like they're about to do something stupid.The other minus is that Bosch's iOS app for connecting with the dishwasher is strange, quirky, and pretty much useless even when it works. It is in fact not working for us after connecting briefly to our machine. We knew to expect this because we also own a Bosch heat pump that uses the same underlying technology and account. This is a shortcoming of Bosch GmBH, and the only inconvenience is being unable to see how much time is left on a dishwashing cycle. (You can always open the door to see the display.)Neither of these points draw away significantly from the fact that ALL our dishes are now getting clean, consistently and thoroughly. The price couldn't be beat, and we're glad to have a worthy replacement for our old Bosch.

In fact, before the dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Both my mom and I are the type of person who needs to wash the dishes right away to relieve our frustration, so we always end up standing around after eating. My dad must have felt sorry for me so he bought me one. Actually, I've used a dishwasher before, but at the time, I bought it not long after dishwashers came out, so I think it was technically an accessory. I ended up not using the dishwasher because the dishes didn't clean well and the grease wasn't removed properly. I remembered that before purchasing it and said I didn't have to buy it, but the girls in my house who were slow-handed were probably frustrated or pitiful so I bought it because they gave me a gold bundle so I had to buy it, but since it requires water, it wasn't arranged as nicely as I wanted. When I returned from work, it was installed like that. I told my mom that I should have installed it straight ahead instead of to the side like this, but she said it was an inevitable choice because of the water. Anyway, the detergent arrived yesterday and I wanted to test it, so I tested it after using a lot of dishwashers, and it wasn't the same as before. It cleans dishes well and removes grease well. However, if you choose the standard course and include hot air drying, it takes almost 2 hours. And if you select hot air drying, the dishwasher will automatically open later. After going for a walk, I went to the dishwasher to see if it had been washed well, but the dishwasher was open. Is this defective? I read other people's reviews and was relieved to hear that the door opens automatically after drying with hot air. I thought it was a defective product and almost opened the lid for a moment. Anyway, I'm going to try my best to use what I bought!

Sentence (English): The inside of this dishwasher is significantly smaller than our Maytag from 2001, and some of the connecting pieces (including the water intake tube) are plastic and will never last as long as our old dishwasher did.
Comments (English): [ I miss our Maytag ] || ---------------- || The inside of this dishwasher is significantly smaller than our Maytag from 2001, and some of the connecting pieces (including the water intake tube) are plastic and will never last as long as our old dishwasher did. The salesman at the store even said “they don't make appliances like they used to, unfortunately. You'll be lucky to get 8-10 years out of any dishwasher made now.” I appreciate the honesty, but it still is awful that you spend $800-$1,000 for something not to last very long. The manufacturers know that they're using cheap parts for these, but they don't care. People will still buy them. That being said, it's about equally as quiet as our old dishwasher. The delivery guys initially took the insulation with them, and I had to make a gazillion phone calls to get them to bring it back. They didn't speak very good English, so I'm not sure they could understand what I was requesting of them. I ended up needing to get in contact with a manager at the store who had to relay the information. Also, loaded the dishwasher for the first time (after our trial run), and didn't use the cover for the silverware. Because they weren't lodged in place, one of the spoons got stuck in a hole during the cycle and scratched the stainless steel when I pulled the bottom rack out. There is literally no room between the door and the bottom rack, so be careful. Our old one at least had a 2 inch gap between.

Sentence (English): I despise this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Washed dishes fine but I despise using it ] || ---------------- || I despise this dishwasher. I have been using it for four months now. The main issue is that the door will not open fully so the bottom rack does not fully deploy. The installers compensated by raising the back feet. Now the bottom rack stays deployed but the top rack slides out on its own. We tried to correct this by zip tying the back of the top rack so that it is more horizontal, but you can't adjust it too much or the water supply in the back doesn't line up and the door won't close. Add to this complaint is that half the time the soap pod is still evident when the cycle is finished, sometimes even entirely there. The cover opens, but it is not flushed out. The third rack is useless since everything ends up wet at the end of the cycle and grease is not washed off of items on the top rack. Finally, GE must have a manufacturing problem since my dishwasher's front panel had to be replaced due to an evident wrinkle when the sheet metal was folded around a corner, and the replacement door was only marginally better. I spent over $1100 buying and having this dishwasher installed. I should have fixed my old Maytag.

Sentence (English): Had a rubbish new Glem dishwasher already installed in a house we moved into 5 years ago.
Comments (English): [ Love the better quality and design ] || ---------------- || Had a rubbish new Glem dishwasher already installed in a house we moved into 5 years ago. After previously owning a Bosch dishwasher I immediately noticed things I didn't like with the other brand, eg:bowls and normal tall std glasses didn't fit in the middle basket as they would hit the cutlery draw and not close. Dropped the middle basket lower, then it would hit the plates on the bottom drawer and not shut either-Just bad design. The dishwashing powder hatch didn't always open, it was noisy, and within 5 years it stopped washing dishes at all. stuffed. Yippee! I wanted to buy another Bosch but felt I should wait til the other one had problems as not to be wasteful. I already had done my homework and knew which one we wanted. This model fits everything exactly where it should go without the drawers being blocked from closing because of bowl or glass heights etc. German design/made. It cleans better with the same powder and rinse aid, and glasses are more sparkling. It is quieter, uses less power and more water efficient. We have solar and I'm starting to see the value in the apps which easily let you choose and remote start the cycle when its sunny and out ie at work. Has a quick 30min wash which cleaned perfectly. It's exactly what I wanted, and by doing my homework first ended up with the best purchase. Wouldn't think you'd get excited about a dishwasher. but this one ticks all my boxes. Thanks GoodGuys!

Sentence (English): We purchased this to replace a failed "high-end' DW from another brand.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We purchased this to replace a failed "high-end' DW from another brand. When we purchased that one, this had been our other leading contender, so it was easy to come to a decision this time. Price points are comparable, as are features. The Crystal Dry feature works well -- dishes are always dry, except for things with areas that collect water (like the bottoms of coffee cups, and plastics with downward-curving rims). The top tray is great. It's adjustable and just a little deeper than the one in our old DW, which allows shallow bowls in addition to utensils, saving space in the main racks. The one disappointment we've found is the racks have angled prongs, and are very difficult to load efficiently. It feels like we have more wasted space and can wash fewer dishes per load than the old DW with vertical prongs. That said, it's hardly a deal-breaker, and we LOVE this DW. Hopefully we'll get a LOT more years' use from it than the old one.

Sentence (English): I bought the LG in May, 2021, together with a 3 year Protection Plan, to replace another brand machine that began to leak as soon as it was installed.
Comments (English): [ Does Not Live Up to Adverts ] || ---------------- || I bought the LG in May, 2021, together with a 3 year Protection Plan, to replace another brand machine that began to leak as soon as it was installed. A major criteria in the selection of the LG was the db rating of 42. Our floorplan is a common, open, Great Room, and I had no desire to listen to a noisy dishwasher while reading or trying to listen to the evening news. For the first 19 months I gave the LG dishwasher a solid B. The only minor complaint being that items placed in the top rack had to be prewashed or they would come out dirty.All this changed when, in January of this 2024, the machine began to make a loud, thumping sound much like a helicopter flying overhead. I submitted a claim to Lowes and within a couple weeks a repairman showed up and announced that the dishwasher needed a new pump. The pump was ordered, and some 2 or 3 weeks after the first visit a second repairman arrived and installed the new pump. The new pump did NOT illuminate the noise. After a couple tense phone calls with the repair service a repairman returned, checked out the dishwasher, and announced that the noise was from the new pump and that the Protection Plan did not cover noise. The dishwasher was cleaning the dishes, end of Protection Plan coverage. I once worked in Seoul, South Korea for a year, and came to appreciate the people, their industry, and was taken by the country's business plan that called for the export of quality products. I am now not all that certain as to their success in this part of their business plan. To purchase a high quality item, paying in excess of $1,000, and have that product fail after only 19 months, and have the Lowes Protection Plan flop as horribly as it did, leaves a very bitter taste in my mouth. As a result I cannot recommend either this dishwasher or the Lowes Protection Plan.

Sentence (English): This is my third dishwasher in the 10 years I have lived in this 1970's house.

I wanted a good/better dishwasher and knew that Bosch would fill the bill if I could just afford it. Lowe's had it on sale and could be delivered the next day. And I have been in dishwasher heaven ever since. Quiet, of course. Gets the dishes clean AND sparkly. My husband has even learned how to turn it on! And most surprising, the Bosch dishwasher sends me a message when it is finished with the load. A very SMART machine. Since I have had it, I have only needed to do two dishwasher loads one day, as it holds so much including odd shaped, large items and other things that I could not put in my other dishwashers.

This all could have been avoided if this information had been communicated up front by either Costco or the delivery company they partner with. Lastly, we then had to put up with multiple phone calls from the delivery company, asking us when we were going to schedule the install. even though they had already refused to do it. Clearly they were not the most organized with updating their records.

Sentence (English): I, the home owner, installed the dishwasher.
Comments (English): I, the home owner, installed the dishwasher. Instructions in the Owners Manual were good but a little vague in spots. The video link via the QR code was very helpful and filled in many of vague spots. One instruction, part of #40, I believe is incorrect. It says that for side anchoring, drill a 7/32" pilot hole in the cabinet. 7/32" is .219" dia which is larger than the thread dia of the #8 screw provided! I used a smaller drill to drill the pilot hole, otherwise there would not have been any wood for the #8 screw to attach to.

Sentence (English): Our new Bosch dishwasher has more than filled the gap left when our old KitchenAid dishwasher bit the dust.
Comments (English): [ Clean and Communicative ] || ---------------- || Our new Bosch dishwasher has more than filled the gap left when our old KitchenAid dishwasher bit the dust. We love the three drawers especially the silverware/flatware drawer on top, which I wasn't sure I would use since there is still a place to put silverware in the bottom drawer. But laying out our flatware in that top drawer is easy to do and makes it even easier to unload at the end of the cycle. The door of the dishwasher pops open at the end of the cycle to help finish the drying. We did remove the Finish/JetDry sticker along the edge of the door as that seemed to keep it from opening at first a few times. But a little sticker peeling and Goo-Gone did the trick. We also have connected to the Home Connect app which has made it fun to name our dishwasher, start our dishwasher and be notified when the cycle is complete. We also love the red light that shines on the floor below the dishwasher which tells us when the dishwasher is operating. We are very happy with our purchase!

Sentence (English): Glad we chose KitchenAid this time around.
Comments (English): [ Have Two in our Remodeled Kitchen - Very Happy ] || ---------------- || Glad we chose KitchenAid this time around. We remodeled our kitchen two years ago to include two dishwashers. Very useful around the holidays and also for large dinner parties. Also, invariably we don't run the DW until it is full and that is always when there are still more dishes from a meal. So, two works well for us. I was so pleased with the performance of this dishwasher that I just purchased another for our second home when our old one threw in the towel. Now the dishwasher itself! Very pleased with the performance. I scape some larger pieces off the dishes but never rinse them first (that is why it is called a dishwasher)! I almost always use the Express wash cycle with dry cycle. Have never had a dirty dish when I unload it. On Express wash some of the plastics may still have a little water especially in the grooves or indentations. That is to be expected. You cannot added extra dry time on the Express cycle - only on the longer cycles. If we have a lot of plastics I will sometimes run the Normal cycle with extended dry and then there is very little water on the plastics - if any. I don't understand the many reviews where there are complaints of dishes not dry. All china and glasses come out bone-dry even on Express. I have never used any of the longer cycles - not sure what the purpose would be. Normal cleans even baked on food from dishes. I don't put pans in the dishwasher so maybe they would required longer cycles - but i doubt it. If we think of it - and are in the kitchen soon after the cycle finishes we do crack the door open - this helps a lot with ensuring everything is dry when you unload - but not really necessary. Also, using the drying agent makes a huge difference. I notice if it runs out that dishes are not as dry. We like the third rack - great for measuring cups, spatulas, etc. The racks are very smooth pulling out and are heavy in construction. The stainless steel interior is great and much nicer that plastic. I think it also aids in drying. We prefer a dishwasher with the bar on the door rather than recessed handle (which looks cleaner) because always a great place to hang towels - which invariably fall of when we open door. Wish there was some type of grip on the back of the handle to hold towels in place. Delay timer is nice feature that I use to delay start time until after peak electric hours. This dishwasher is SILENT! You actually have to feel it to be sure it is running. Only thing I wish they would add is a Dry Only cycle - to heat dishes before serving - but have yet to see it on any dishwasher.

I was so pleased with the performance of this dishwasher that I just purchased another for our second home when our old one threw in the towel.Now the dishwasher itself! Very pleased with the performance.  I scape some larger pieces off the dishes but never rinse them first (that is why it is called a dishwasher)!  I almost always use the Express wash cycle with dry cycle.  Have never had a dirty dish when I unload it.  On Express wash some of the plastics may still have a little water especially in the grooves or indentations.  That is to be expected.  You cannot added extra dry time on the Express cycle - only on the longer cycles. If we have a lot of plastics I will sometimes run the Normal cycle with extended dry and then there is very little water on the plastics - if any.  I don't understand the many reviews where there are complaints of dishes not dry.  All china and glasses come out bone-dry even on Express.  I have never used any of the longer cycles - not sure what the purpose would be.  Normal cleans even baked on food from dishes.  I don't put pans in the dishwasher so maybe they would required longer cycles - but i doubt it.  If we think of it - and are in the kitchen soon after the cycle finishes we do crack the door open - this helps a lot with ensuring everything is dry when you unload - but not really necessary.  Also, using the drying agent makes a huge difference.  I notice if it runs out that dishes are not as dry.We like the third rack - great for measuring cups, spatulas, etc. The racks are very smooth pulling out and are heavy in construction.  The stainless steel interior  is great and much nicer that plastic.  I think it also aids in drying.  We prefer a dishwasher with the bar on the door rather than recessed handle (which looks cleaner) because always a great place to hang towels - which invariably fall of when we open door.  Wish there was some type of grip on the back of the handle to hold towels in place. Delay timer is nice feature that I use to delay start time until after peak electric hours.  This dishwasher is SILENT!  You actually have to feel it to be sure it is running.  Only thing I wish they would add is a Dry Only cycle - to heat dishes before serving - but have yet to see it on any dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I didn't think such a thing existed as "the perfect dishwasher" but I'm a believer now.
Comments (English): [ The Perfect Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I didn't think such a thing existed as "the perfect dishwasher" but I'm a believer now. I bought my Bosch to replace a Kenmore Elite and I haven't looked back since. I made a list before buying of what I actually wanted a dishwasher to do not sure if I would find one to fit the bill. First of all I wanted a dishwasher that would actually clean the dishes without my pre washing everything first. Second I wanted a dishwasher that actually dried the dishes. Rather basic but still sometimes difficult to find. The extras would be no etching of glassware with my hard water, wheels that stayed on the racks, and quiet performance as our living room is right off the kitchen. I got all that and more. This dishwasher has a built in water softener so no more etching of glassware. It actually dries the dishes AND plastic ware! Not only does it dry the plastic but I can load it on any rack as there is no heating element to melt and deform the plastic. The dishwasher is so quiet that the only way I know it is running is to look at the display showing how much time is left for the cycle. The interior light is a bonus and having it connected to my phone to remind me of rinse aid getting low, etc is also a plus. If the longevity of this dishwasher is good (I've only had mine a couple of months) then I would call it the perfect dishwasher! The engineers got it right!

I bought my Bosch to replace a Kenmore Elite and I haven't looked back since. I made a list before buying of what I actually wanted a dishwasher to do not sure if I would find one to fit the bill. First of all I wanted a dishwasher that would actually clean the dishes without my pre washing everything first. Second I wanted a dishwasher that actually dried the dishes. Rather basic but still sometimes difficult to find. The extras would be no etching of glassware with my hard water, wheels that stayed on the racks, and quiet performance as our living room is right off the kitchen. I got all that and more. This dishwasher has a built in water softener so no more etching of glassware. It actually dries the dishes AND plastic ware! Not only does it dry the plastic but I can load it on any rack as there is no heating element to melt and deform the plastic. The dishwasher is so quiet that the only way I know it is running is to look at the display showing how much time is left for the cycle. The interior light is a bonus and having it connected to my phone to remind me of rinse aid getting low, etc is also a plus. If the longevity of this dishwasher is good (I've only had mine a couple of months) then I would call it the perfect dishwasher! The engineers got it right!

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher a little bit ago and have only ran it once.
Comments (English): [ Very nice ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher a little bit ago and have only ran it once. Pros: Third rack, Leak detection system, It's very quiet (especially compared to my last one), Cleans well, and I like that the silverware caddy in the bottom rack comes apart. Cons (disclaimer I've only run the DW once so far) There's not as much flexibility with the lower rack with flipping down the plate holders/dividers as I'd like. If you're using regular plates most of the time, this dishwasher is fine, but I use a lot of Tupperware, which really only fits along the perimeter of the dishwasher. Or going sideways between the tines which takes up more space. It would be nice if some of the dividers let you push down like half the tines to accommodate the wider width of most Tupperware going the "right way" between tines. While I do like that the silverware caddy comes apart, it would be nice if the individual compartments could stand on their own better. The middle part is fine, but the two end pieces don't really stand on their own unless you balance it really well with silverware or have it in the right spot. It would also be nice if I could rearrange them since they come apart, to like have what's supposed to be the middle part in the back and then the two end pieces in the front. My only other partial complaint is that it didn't dry well on the sensor cycle. I have only run it once, so I will have to try the extended dry feature or play around to make sure things dry completely and I don't have to leave the door open for a day for everything to dry out. But overall, this dishwasher is very nice and a huge improvement over my last one.

Sentence (English): After a lot of research, we found that Whirlpool [a "good old" company] was given high ratings.
Comments (English): [ Good features, 3 racks but an odd spacing of posts ] || ---------------- || After a lot of research, we found that Whirlpool [a "good old" company] was given high ratings. So we got this, thinking it would be a great fit especially because of the 3rd rack. [no need 2 for silverware trays] Unfortunately, the top tray is too close to the top to fit much and only it can't be lowered. Then, after the first wash I had to scrub some ceramic casseroles, that weren't cleaned. I don't think the heating element [if there is one] works well. And everything was really wet when the cycle was done & left spots. Also I thought I'd have enough room, with all the posts, to put my dishes in, but the bottom rack's 3 sections are too close & the posts too far apart to fit all we [2 of us] the dishes we use. I also thought I'd be able to put my pots in, but if I do that, then I can't sufficiently fill the dishwasher. So far, we aren't thrilled, though it is Much better than doing dishes by hand! Too, I'm not impressed with your operating instructions, the photos/drawings are too small to see. But, we shall see . maybe over time it will do a better job [& hopefully it was connected properly.]* First, We now have a problem with another Whirlpool. WE bought a Refrigerator on 03/08/202: Model # WRQA59NKZ; Serial # TMB*******, because it had double doors rather than the deep drawer ones. Like it a lot, [even though the freezer space is a bit lacking, due to the extra wide "side sliders" of the freezer drawers].> But, I just noticed the "seal" on the bottom, right side of the refrigerator has torn. I don't know how it could have happened, or if this can be fixed, or what if anything can be done. But it seems to be a very flimsy rubber flap. Maybe the left side closes too tight, or ? Can this be fixed or what can be done, if anything? * Second, we got it with an "ice maker" - but since we can't connect it to a water supply. I don't know if it could be taken out without damaging the freezer [or if it could have come without one. Salesman didn't ask & I didn't think of it.] I hope someone can help us with this tell us what can be done, as removing it would greatly add to the freezer space. Please advise on these 2 items. Thanks n vada con dio a tutti.

Sentence (English): I am extremely happy with my new Whirlpool dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Wonderful Dishwasher-100% Satisfied ] || ---------------- || I am extremely happy with my new Whirlpool dishwasher. It does an excellent job, has wonderful features and had a very reasonable price. I have zero complaints. I typically use the sensor cycle and heated dry. Plastic storage containers are always clean but there can be water in in any upturned grooves molded into the container. I do not see this as a problem, all dishwashers have drying issues with plastic. I did a great deal of research and talked to many friends and family members about their dishwasher experiences. Many people complained about glasses and dishes (not just plastic) not being dry when the machine is done. This includes expensive high end brands like Bosch. I decided heated drying was a "must have" feature. Whirlpool has it and my dishes are always dry. My unit has the edge mounted controls. I was a little leery about this feature, but now I like it. It turned out to be much easier to use than I expected, and the front of the dishwasher is easier to clean. My model has the deep third rack. I love it! It easily holds small dishes, coffee cups and cocktail glasses. As well as kitchen utensils. What I put in the third rack is always perfectly clean. I paid more specifically for this feature and am happy I did it. The silverware basket has lids with openings designed to keep silverware separated to ensure they are completely cleaned. It works very well. A big improvement from my last dishwasher. The overall capacity of my new dishwasher is much more than my previous one. It is also very quiet. I use the time delayed start feature. I can't tell when it starts. I am very impressed. I installed the dishwasher myself. The installation instructions and the video (link in the manual) are very well done. I had no trouble at all installing the unit. I will note, the new dishwasher is a bit taller and a bit wider than my old one. I had to do a little cabinet work to allow for this. Based on my research, any new dishwasher would have required this work. I have an old house, I suspect newer kitchens are designed for the larger dishwashers. Model I purchased: WDPA70SAMZMy last dishwasher was a WhirlPool. It did a great job and lasted 25 years. I am looking forward to a similar experience.

Comments (English): [ Exceptional Cleaning Performance with Some Quirks ] || ---------------- || Having used this dishwasher for nearly a month now, I must admit it surpasses any other dishwasher I've owned in terms of cleaning prowess. It tackles dirt and grime with ease, leaving dishes sparkling clean and eliminating the need for pre-rinsing. This alone makes it a winner in my book. However, there are a few drawbacks that prevent it from being perfect. The most notable issue is its drying function. While the dishes come out clean, achieving dryness requires utilizing the extra dry function coupled with the nighttime cycle. Another minor gripe is the seemingly smaller baskets, or perhaps they just hold less, though I can't quite pinpoint the exact reason for this perception. Nonetheless, it does pose a slight inconvenience, particularly when loading larger items. On a positive note, I appreciate the inclusion of the small basket at the top, which is perfect for organizing wooden spoons, knives, and my wife's chopsticks. It's these little details that demonstrate thoughtful design elements. In summary, while this dishwasher excels in its primary function of cleaning dishes, its design leaves a bit to be desired. The need for extra drying steps and the slightly smaller baskets detract from an otherwise outstanding appliance. Despite these drawbacks, I remain extremely satisfied with its cleaning performance; considering its price point, it is a worthwhile investment for any household. LDTS5552S. Sentence (English): You won't believe how dishes and glasses sparkle when you take them out of this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Spectacular cleaning, weird racks ] || ---------------- || You won't believe how dishes and glasses sparkle when you take them out of this dishwasher. It's quiet and incredibly effective, and for those reasons we love it so far. I don't think it dries as well as my older one, despite the \"crystal\" technology, but that doesn't bother us too much. It dries well enough. Where we're a little confused is the racks, especially the second, top rack where we put glasses and bowls. There doesn't seem to be any way to position glasses so they won't bump against each other every time you pull the rack out and in. It's like the wild west up there, unlike our old one of a different brand which had spines in the right places and kept everything orderly. The bottom rack spines are very close together which worried me at first, but the dishes come out clean anyway so maybe that just saves a ton of space. So I'm docking a star for that strange second rack, unless someone can show me a system that I'm missing. But for cleaning and shine, I doubt you can beat this machine.
